chapters.title: Social Issues in the United States
chapters.text:
Students explore major social challenges in the U.S., examining data, media representations, and engaging in structured debates on abortion and capital punishment.

Compétences visées :
• Analyze written documents and media sources
• Identify key statistics and trends
• Express opinions about controversial topics

Contenus du programme :
• Statistical overview of poverty, homelessness, and abortion in the U.S.
• Analysis of news articles, magazines, and internet reports
• Debate on the pros and cons of abortion and the death penalty
competences: Analyze written documents and media sources
contenus: Statistical overview of poverty, homelessness, and abortion in the U.S.
Analysis of news articles, magazines, and internet reports
Debate on the pros and cons of abortion and the death penalty
chapters.summary: Students explore major social challenges in the U.S., examining data, media representations, and engaging in structured debates on abortion and capital punishment.

chapters.title: Human Rights and the Death Penalty
chapters.text:
Through comparative study and debate, students critically assess the death penalty's ethical, legal, and human rights dimensions.

Compétences visées :
• Compare and contrast legal frameworks
• Evaluate arguments for and against the death penalty
• Support positions with evidence

Contenus du programme :
• Comparative analysis of death penalty laws in different countries
• Human rights implications of capital punishment
• Student debate: Adoption of the death penalty vs. life imprisonment
competences: Evaluate arguments for and against the death penalty
contenus: Comparative analysis of death penalty laws in different countries
Human rights implications of capital punishment
Student debate: Adoption of the death penalty vs. life imprisonment
chapters.summary: Through comparative study and debate, students critically assess the death penalty's ethical, legal, and human rights dimensions.

chapters.title: Urban Life and Homelessness in Haiti
chapters.text:
Students gather first‑hand data on Haitian homelessness, analyze urban challenges, and develop actionable solutions to improve community well‑being.

Compétences visées :
• Conduct field surveys
• Propose realistic solutions to social problems
• Analyze urban vs rural living conditions

Contenus du programme :
• Survey design and data collection on homelessness in an urban area
• Presentation of findings and proposed interventions
• Discussion on advantages and disadvantages of city life
competences: Propose realistic solutions to social problems
Analyze urban vs rural living conditions
contenus: Survey design and data collection on homelessness in an urban area
Presentation of findings and proposed interventions
Discussion on advantages and disadvantages of city life
chapters.summary: Students gather first‑hand data on Haitian homelessness, analyze urban challenges, and develop actionable solutions to improve community well‑being.

chapters.title: Grammar Focus I: Adjectives, Possessives, and Comparatives
chapters.text:
Students strengthen foundational grammar skills, enabling clearer expression of descriptions, ownership, and comparisons in English.

Compétences visées :
• Identify and use adjectives in correct positions
• Apply possessive forms in sentences
• Construct comparative and superlative adjectives

Contenus du programme :
• Adjective placement rules and examples
• Formation of the possessive case (’s, s’) in various contexts
• Exercises on comparative and superlative forms
competences: Identify and use adjectives in correct positions
contenus: Formation of the possessive case (’s, s’) in various contexts
Exercises on comparative and superlative forms
chapters.summary: Students strengthen foundational grammar skills, enabling clearer expression of descriptions, ownership, and comparisons in English.

chapters.title: Grammar Focus II: Auxiliary Verbs, Question Tags, and Relative Clauses
chapters.text:
This unit deepens students’ grammatical precision, supporting more complex sentence structures and nuanced communication.

Compétences visées :
• Recognize and employ auxiliary verbs
• Generate appropriate question tags
• Construct relative clauses to add detail

Contenus du programme :
• Usage of auxiliary verbs (do/does, have/has, will, can, etc.)
• Practice forming question tags in dialogue
• Building relative clauses to modify nouns
competences: Construct relative clauses to add detail
contenus: Usage of auxiliary verbs (do/does, have/has, will, can, etc.)
Practice forming question tags in dialogue
Building relative clauses to modify nouns
chapters.summary: This unit deepens students’ grammatical precision, supporting more complex sentence structures and nuanced communication.

chapters.title: Cultural Perspectives on Termination of Pregnancy
chapters.text:
Students investigate how cultural, religious, and legal factors shape attitudes toward abortion, fostering critical thinking and respectful dialogue.

Compétences visées :
• Analyze cultural attitudes toward abortion
• Discuss freedom of choice in different societies
• Present balanced viewpoints respectfully

Contenus du programme :
• Cultural contexts: Haiti, U.S., and other selected countries
• Historical evolution of abortion laws and public opinion
• Student presentations on cultural influences and personal reflections
competences: Discuss freedom of choice in different societies
contenus: Cultural contexts: Haiti, U.S., and other selected countries
Historical evolution of abortion laws and public opinion
Student presentations on cultural influences and personal reflections
chapters.summary: Students investigate how cultural, religious, and legal factors shape attitudes toward abortion, fostering critical thinking and respectful dialogue.
